mechanism: GameState.frame returns raw.frame[-1] ('the final visible frame'). On an ordinary step raw.frame holds one layer, the board. On the step that COMPLETES a level it holds two or more: layer 0 is the terminal board of the level just cleared, layer[-1] is the opening board of the NEXT level. Every reader in the duck/taaf lineage (.ascii, .segmentation, all grafts, and our own EXEC-WM settled-frame reader at duck_eval/execwm/ewm_smoke.py:328) takes the last layer, so at the single instant that carries the only ground truth the game volunteers about its objective, the agent is handed the next level's board labelled as the result of its winning action. For EXEC-WM specifically this makes the PHASE P predict-act-compare check mispredict by construction at every level clear, which the sealed prereg charges as a BREAK; MAX_BREAKS_PER_LEVEL=3 then latches fallback and D3's levels_cleared_by_plan under-counts.
summary: Claim published in thtennant/arc3-duck-v25 (winframe graft, 2026-08-25) and INDEPENDENTLY REPLICATED by us the same night, offline, on data/human_replays/*.jsonl across 6 games with recorded level wins. Every level-win step in all six games carries extra frame layers. lp85: 1 layer on 416/424 ordinary steps, 2 layers on 7/8 wins; prev-board vs layer0 = 288 cells differ, vs layer[-1] = 1505. ar25: 1 layer on 570/579 ordinary, 3 at wins; prev vs layer0 = 105, vs layer[-1] = 692, and layer[-1] vs the NEXT step's board = 0 cells (bit-identical). cd82: 1 layer on 110/138, 15-16 at wins; prev vs layer0 = 1 cell, vs layer[-1] = 410. Layer 0 is the winning action's actual result; layer[-1] is the next level's start. Same night, our EXEC-WM v1 arm drew a board-verified 1.05 (z=-1.94 vs field floor n=5 mean 1.5760 sd 0.2713; z=+0.67 vs frozen-fork null n=37 0.9316/0.1771, i.e. inside the null). The defect is a candidate mechanical cause of that draw and MUST be checked in the pulled artifact before the prereg's decisive-kill clause is allowed to fire.
lesson: An instrument audit is only as wide as the cases it covered. Our 2026-08-24 brief answered the film-strip finding with 'our lineage already reads raw.frame[-1] -- audited, no defect'; that audit tested animation strips MID-LEVEL and never tested a level TRANSITION, which is the one place where reading [-1] is the defect. The conclusion outran the test's scope and would have been used to license a decisive kill of a whole rule class. Two rules follow: (1) when an audit clears an accessor, record which state transitions it actually exercised, and treat untested transitions as unaudited rather than as clean; (2) a losing draw from a new arm is not a verdict until its own instruments are checked -- a mis-instrumented run cannot kill a rule class. Extends feedback_audit_the_instrument and the arm-mismatch scorer lesson.
